statement: Whether Coronelli's southern coast derives from the Ortelius generation or from a later reduced outline is not established.
notes: Blocked by ant-gap-coronelli-gores. Recorded as a question so that Act III cannot answer it by assumption.

statement: The relationship between Coronelli's globe and the Mercator southern outline is not established.
notes: A globe and a wall map answer different design constraints, so a resemblance would need argument even if one were found. Blocked by ant-gap-coronelli-gores: these are questions about the globe, and no gore set has been examined.

feature: Tierra del Fuego and the southern strait
statement: Whether Coronelli detaches Tierra del Fuego from a southern landmass, as later seventeenth-century mapping increasingly did, has not been checked.
notes: The clearest single test of whether Coronelli is inheriting or updating, and therefore the first thing to look at when the gores are examined. Blocked by ant-gap-coronelli-gores: these are questions about the globe, and no gore set has been examined.

statement: The Atlante Veneto Tomo I polar section carries two engraved plates, 'Terre Artiche' and 'Polo Artiche', both wholly Arctic; the six text leaves are headed for both poles but no southern polar plate was cut.
notes: Established 2026-08-25 by examining Rumsey 12186.101 at full resolution and reading the catalogue sequence .100 to .108 item by item. 'direct_observation' here classifies our examination of the object, not a seventeenth-century observation of the Arctic; the vocabulary has no separate class for a bibliographic fact and the reading is recorded here so it is auditable. This is Act III's finding rather than an obstacle to it.

statement: Whatever Coronelli shows in the far south is bounded, and largely removed, by the tracks on the 1777 chart.
notes: The one lineage link whose later term is a verified object. It still cannot be drawn until the Coronelli end of it is known.

statement: The central legend of 'Terre Artiche' cites Hugh Willoughby ('Vgone Willogheo'), English, at latitude 76 degrees, and a party of seven sent to overwinter at Spitsbergen to test the China passage, which sailed 30 August 1633 and returned without profit 26 May 1634.
notes: Read from the plate at full IIIF resolution 2026-08-25. Reported rather than observed or inherited: Coronelli is relaying other men's voyages with names, dates and latitudes attached. The crop clipped the left margin, so line openings were not read and no continuous transcription is claimed.

statement: The same legend cites Friedrich Martens of Hamburg, who sailed from the Elbe 15 April 1671, pushed through ice toward Spitsbergen and returned 21 August the same year having reached 81 degrees.
notes: Read from the plate at full IIIF resolution 2026-08-25. The northern legend is a voyage register, not a cosmography: this is the evidential material the southern half of the section header has no equivalent of.
